misconceptions.description: Reducing UDL to offering the same content in several formats, ignoring the engagement and action-and-expression principles.
misconceptions.trigger: learner claims a design is UDL because it provides video, text, and audio of the same material
misconceptions.feedback: Multiple formats address representation only. Add options for engagement (the why) and for action and expression (the how) to cover all three UDL principles.

misconceptions.description: Believing UDL flexibility means lowering or changing the learning goal for some learners rather than varying the means to a firm goal.
misconceptions.trigger: learner reduces the standard or swaps the construct instead of varying how it is demonstrated
misconceptions.feedback: Keep goals firm and means flexible. Vary how learners engage, access, and demonstrate the same construct; do not lower the goal.

misconceptions.description: Treating UDL as reactive individual accommodations added later by request, rather than proactive design for predictable variability.
misconceptions.trigger: learner plans to add options later only for students who ask
misconceptions.feedback: UDL designs for the margins from the start. Build flexible options into the design proactively rather than retrofitting them for individuals.
